in.role: Baltimore's only pass-catching TE — Likely and Kolar both left, Smythe is a blocker

out.role: RB5 in Arizona, 42% rostered, no path to touches

doFirst.why: Pitts catches passes from Cooper Rush today. Tua is out with an oblique, Rush was QB3 until Thursday and is himself dealing with back spasms, Atlanta's pass rate was cut from 58.5% to 55.5%, and the right tackle is banged up against a Steelers front that returns every starter. Andrews goes the other way: Likely and Kolar are gone, he is close to an every-snap player for the first time in years, he has been top-ten in end-zone targets seven seasons running, and Indianapolis allowed the second-most yards and seventh-most points to tight ends last season. ESPN has them 10.1 to 9.8 — the reporting widens that gap in Andrews' favour, and Andrews costs nothing because he is a free agent.

action.label: Add Mark Andrews, drop Tyler Allgeier — then start Andrews at TE over Pitts

candidates.note: Jakobi Meyers is 79% rostered across ESPN and sitting here as a free agent. Over the back half of last season, with Brian Thomas Jr. healthy and on the field, Meyers was the WR28 in points per game on a 22.6% target share and a 26.7% first-read share — he was functionally Jacksonville's number one, not their number two. The thumb he jammed is a non-issue; he told reporters himself he is playing. He is not a Week 1 start over what you already have, but he is the best free agent in this league and the one most likely to be gone by Tuesday.

Michael Mayer's ownership moved +2.54 in a day — every other player on this wire moved less than half a point, in either direction. The reason is Brock Bowers, who had a meniscus trim and is reported out one to two games, which makes Mayer the Raiders' starting tight end against Miami. He is 27% rostered. If you do not take the Andrews card above, Mayer is the cheaper version of the same idea; if you do, he is the tight end to watch when Andrews' bye or a Pitts rebound forces a decision.
